newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada regulators set Sable natural gas hearing.
newsitem.headline: Canada regulators set Sable natural gas hearing.

text.p: The Canadian Joint Public Review Panel for the Sable Gas Projects said on Tuesday it would hold a public hearing in April to review proposals for developing the C$3 billion offshore Nova Scotia Sable gas project.

The panel, which includes representatives from the governments of Canada and Nova Scotia, the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Board and the National Energy Board, are slated to review proposals to develop Sable's six offshore natural gas fields and build a gas plant, storage facilities and pipeline in Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, it said.
Plans for the project's development include:

- a proposal by Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada, Shell Canada Ltd, Imperial Oil Ltd and Nova Scotia Resources to develop the fields and build a pipeline to shore, a plant at Goldboro, Nova Scotia, a pipeline to ship gas liquids to Point Tupper, Nova Scotia from the plant and storage facilities at Point Tupper. Estimated production for the fields would be 400 million cubic feet per day of gas.
